verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's first-party docs cover the built-in accessibility tools: a getting-started guide for the screen reader, reading the screen aloud and in Braille, contrast, text size and magnification controls, and keyboard navigation with bounce, slow and sticky keys. Together these show the OS ships a built-in screen reader and a broad accessibility toolkit. Missing for 10: evidence that accessibility tools work during installation and first-run setup, and independent or hands-on corroboration of screen-reader quality.
